analysis.title: Americas Retail: Retail sales in line with consensus in October, September restated slightly higher
key_insights: October headline retail sales rose +0.2% m/m. That is below the GS estimate of +0.3% and in line with Reuters consensus of +0.2%.
September headline retail sales were restated to +0.83% m/m from +0.77%. September y/y growth was restated to +6.5% from +6.3%, and core y/y to +6.3% from +5.5%.
Headline retail sales grew +6.8% y/y in October (vs. +2.8% in Oct'25 and +6.5% in Sept'26). The 2-year stack was +9.6%, down from +10.2% in September.
Core retail sales (ex-auto, food and gas) grew +6.6% y/y in October (vs. +6.3% in September) and about +0.8% m/m. The 2-year stack rose to +10.2% from +9.8%.
Total ex-auto rose +0.6% m/m in October against +0.4% for both consensus and GS. The y/y rate was +7.9% vs. +7.6% restated in September.

Seven of 15 categories accelerated y/y versus September: miscellaneous, gas stations, auto parts, DIY, health & personal, non-store and food services. Seven also accelerated on a 2-year stack, led by miscellaneous at +24.1% vs. +17.9%.
Gas stations grew +29.3% y/y in October (+27.2% in September) and +1.5% m/m. Miscellaneous grew +13.4% y/y and +4.7% m/m. Non-store grew +11.1% y/y and +1.2% m/m.
Department stores fell -0.6% y/y in October vs. +5.0% in September, and the y/y change swung by -5.6 points. Furniture and home furnishings slowed to +2.4% y/y from +7.2% and fell -2.3% m/m.
Apparel slowed to +3.3% y/y from +5.4%, and sales were -0.7% m/m. Sporting goods slowed to +7.6% y/y from +10.2%, and electronics & appliances slowed to +7.7% from +8.9%.
Motor vehicle & parts grew +1.9% y/y, with sales -1.6% m/m and the 2-year stack down to +2.9% from +7.0%. Auto parts grew +9.7% y/y, but -0.1% m/m.
Building materials & garden accelerated to +5.7% y/y from +4.2% and was +0.5% m/m. Health & personal turned positive at +0.6% y/y vs. -0.7% in September.

macro_indicators.interpretation: In line with consensus and slightly below the GS estimate of +0.3%. Sequential growth slowed from +0.83% in September (restated).
